instruction: I changed my terminal color scheme to 'Solarized dark' but after rebooting, it reverts back to default. Help me make this color scheme setting permanent.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5);

import pyautogui; import time; time.sleep(0.5); pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 'alt', 't'); time.sleep(1); pyautogui.write('PROFILE=$(gsettings get org.gnome.Terminal.ProfilesList default | tr -d "''\''\''"); echo "use-theme-colors:"; gsettings get org.gnome.Terminal.Legacy.Profile:/org/gnome/terminal/legacy/profiles:/:$PROFILE/ use-theme-colors; echo "background-color:"; gsettings get org.gnome.Terminal.Legacy.Profile:/org/gnome/terminal/legacy/profiles:/:$PROFILE/ background-color; echo "foreground-color:"; gsettings get org.gnome.Terminal.Legacy.Profile:/org/gnome/terminal/legacy/profiles:/:$PROFILE/ foreground-color'); time.sleep(0.5); pyautogui.press('enter')

metadata.explanation: Task requires user to persistently set terminal color scheme to Solarized dark. The evaluator opens a new terminal and checks if use-theme-colors is set to false (which means custom colors are used). Expected output should contain 'false' indicating custom color scheme is active. Similar pattern to original task (checking terminal configuration persistence).
metadata.verification: Verified that gsettings command will check use-theme-colors=false and specific Solarized dark color values (background=#002b36, foreground=#839496). The postconfig queries multiple settings to confirm the exact color scheme is configured, not just any custom color scheme.

llm_judge_reasons: Complete semantic verification: Evaluator correctly checks all three critical settings for Solarized dark: use-theme-colors=false, background-color=#002b36, foreground-color=#839496
Correct color values: Expected values match the official Solarized dark palette (background #002b36 is Solarized dark base03, foreground #839496 is base0)
Proper persistence verification: Postconfig reopens a new terminal to verify settings persist after the user completes the task
Correct metric logic: Metric function properly handles expected.type='rule' by directly accessing expected.get('include', []) without nesting under 'rules' key
Distinguishes specific scheme: By checking specific hex color values, evaluator can distinguish Solarized dark from other custom color schemes (Monokai, Dracula, etc.)
Robust implementation: Getter extracts terminal output, metric performs string matching for all required values with both include/exclude patterns
